analysis.title: Market Update
key_insights: Democrats won majorities in both the House and the Senate in the US midterm elections. The Senate majority is narrow. Democrats won in traditionally Republican regions, including Texas (Republican for nearly forty years) and Kansas (nearly 100 years).
The last time a sitting president lost control of both chambers of Congress was 20 years ago. The White House has said it is willing to work constructively with the Democrats.

Initial market reaction: equities, US Treasuries and gold are higher, and the USD is lower. Markets assume the new situation could slow some market-friendly initiatives of the administration, while greater budget and debt discipline could support bonds.

The White House is expected to rely more on executive orders, especially on trade policy. These orders often end up in court and are overturned. The President has announced he will use vetoes, and Vontobel expects many initiatives to be blocked.

Democrats are likely to open investigations into alleged personal enrichment, government contracting and conflicts of interest. Some political analysts flag a risk of renewed escalation in the Middle East before the new Congress is seated in January 2027.

Vontobel says US equities have often produced positive returns in the 12 months after midterm elections, observed in all midterms since World War II. It cautions that history does not allow conclusions about future performance.

A Democratic Congress could slow growth through more regulation and tighter spending and fewer tax breaks. A slowdown would also dampen inflation. Cost of living and the fight against inflation stay high on the political agenda.
Even with Treasuries trading at higher prices (lower yields), money markets still expect the Fed to raise rates before the end of the year.
Greater budget discipline raises the chance of a government shutdown. Markets seem accustomed to the recurring situation, but it brings uncertainty.

Sector risks: regulation of artificial intelligence, banking and healthcare is expected to come onto the agenda. A rollback of the administration's healthcare measures could matter for Swiss pharmaceutical companies. Environmental and energy policy could affect AI data centers.
Vontobel keeps its preference for equities, implemented through emerging markets, citing growth potential at moderate valuations.
Vontobel keeps an overweight in gold, as a diversifier and because gold could recover with inflation declining and rates expected to fall in the medium term.
Both overweights are funded by an underweight in corporate bonds, where credit spreads remain relatively low. Vontobel also recommends high diversification and a focus on stable income sources.
Vontobel remains constructive on financial markets over the coming months. Near-term focus issues are the Middle East, oil prices, inflation and cost of living.

tension_points.bull_case: Vontobel notes US equities have often risen in the 12 months after midterms. Uncertainty dissipates, and a stalemate means fewer political experiments and greater budget discipline.
tension_points.bear_case: A Democratic Congress could slow growth through more regulation, tighter spending and fewer tax breaks, and the fight against inflation tightens refinancing conditions.
